Definitions & limits

The determinant is shown for a single-component knot. Fox colorings include the three constant colorings; “nonconstant” means at least two colors are used. Coloring and determinant calculations support up to 200 crossings.

Jones uses V(unknot) = 1 and V(t) = (−A³)−w(D)⟨D⟩ with A = t−1/4. Exact state expansion supports up to 18 crossings. Link polynomials may have half-integer powers.

Methods: Kauffman: Jones polynomial; Kolay: coloring matrices; linking numbers.

Import a knot

Use [[a,b,c,d], …] or PD[X[a,b,c,d], …]. Start with the incoming understrand, then list the remaining arcs counterclockwise. Supports up to 80 crossings.

How to use

Move Drag a strand to move it and the surrounding curve. Small empty R1 loops nearby straighten as you drag. Turn off “Loosen small R1 loops while dragging” to keep them. Drag an empty area to pan; use the wheel to zoom.

Draw Draw a stroke to create a closed curve. With auto-close off, strokes remain open; continue from an endpoint to complete a loop. Self-crossings alternate, and new curves pass over existing strands.

Smooth corners Continuing from an endpoint joins smoothly in the existing direction. Closing a curve trims any overshoot, and small hooks at the start or end of a stroke are removed. Use “Smooth sharp corners” on an existing diagram.

Eraser Erase stroke removes an entire curve; Erase segment removes only the part you touch. Rejoining a cut curve preserves the over/under assignments of surviving crossings. Open curves are excluded from calculations.

Lasso Whole curves selects each curve with more than half its length enclosed. Region cuts out and selects only the enclosed portions. Drag to move the selection or use the round handle above it to rotate, with gentle snapping every 15°; hold Shift for 15° steps. Use the floating menu to copy, cut, delete, or paste. Crossings within the selection keep their over/under assignments; at new crossings with other curves, the moved selection passes over.

Switch crossing Tap a crossing to swap its over/under strands.

Auto-relax Strands repel one another to spread out the diagram, using only Reidemeister moves.

Blocked moves Moves are blocked when an R2 removal has different overstrands at its two crossings, an R3 triangle has cyclic over/under ordering, or one strand would pass through another.
